The local host reuses its host-only local-turn publication and persistence path, independently of Agent Merge's controller. An idle chat receives the notice immediately; a busy chat receives it after its active turn finishes, without interrupting that turn or replacing a draft. Notices remain in restored history but never become provider/model requests. Routine polling and unchanged blocked states do not create transcript notices.

-Consecutive notices of the same artifact merge into one. Notices carry their rule changes and each integration's enabled rules in VS Code `_meta`, and the host renders a structured notice from them rather than from client-supplied text, so a notice reads the same before and after it is merged. While the chat's last turn is the artifact's previous notice, the host replaces that turn with a notice that keeps only the latest change of each rule and the latest enabled rules of each integration. A single change keeps its specific title; several are summarized as "Autopilot updated for {artifact} ({n} rules)", with each rule and its explanation in the expandable details. Any other turn in between, such as an agent response, a user message, or another artifact's notice, starts a new notice, as does a merge that would exceed the limits that notice readers accept, and notices deferred during a turn merge before they are written. The replacement uses standard truncation and turn actions, so the host's state and every snapshot contain one notice. The replacement turn's message names the turn it replaces; VS Code clients remove that request when they apply the replacement, in order with other server-initiated requests. Older clients that do not read this name show both notices until the chat is reloaded. Notices from clients that send only rendered content are posted unchanged and never merged.

Prompt-backed actions also have a generic request presentation. After preparation, the executor captures the action label, integration, manual/automatic source, resource presentation, and the currently available details linked to that action or its automation option. A prepared prompt may instead supply the details it is about, such as only the failing checks a CI repair asks to fix; these replace the linked details in the snapshot and are not part of the model-facing prompt. This immutable snapshot is persisted with the run before submission and transported in the optional, validated `vscode.artifactIntegrationRequest` message metadata. Capturing details does not retain observations or fetch additional pages; incomplete or failed captures remain explicit. The snapshot never becomes an instruction or grants execution authority. While a prompt action's turn reports no activity of its own, the host describes it in the session summary by the action's optional `activityLabel`, such as "Fixing CI", or else its label, prefixed with Autopilot when an Autopilot rule ran it.
